- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  Line or code reference: is_limit_wait docstring at line 390, module docstring at lines 82-93
  PROBLEM: The docstrings claim that “not waiting” constructions do not qualify as deferrals, but the implementation accepts multi-word negations.
  WHY: The documentation misleads maintainers about which negated phrases the implementation rejects.
- Requirement: “a retry, resend, resume, or try counts only when the text defers it to the reset (a wait word, until, till, later, or the limit resets; 'not waiting' does not), so 'Usage limit reached. Please retry the request' stays a request” (PR description, Approach step 2 in the plan, AD-7 in the progress log)
  Expected change site: is_limit_wait in both workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py and .claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py — the LIMIT_DEFERRAL_PATTERN check must structurally tie the deferral word to the retry verb rather than accepting any occurrence anywhere in the text
  Evidence of absence: The current LIMIT_DEFERRAL_PATTERN is an unanchored regex search — it accepts "Usage limit reached. Please retry the request. The limit resets later." because "resets" and "later" exist anywhere in the text, in a separate clause. The requirement says the retry must be "deferred to the reset" but the implementation accepts any deferral word in any position, including in an unrelated clause describing the limit's own schedule. The negative lookbehind guard on "not waiting" is also insufficient — it only blocks "not <word>" literal adjacency, not multi-word negations like "not waiting until".
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- Requirement: "tests/test_usage_limit_resumes.py pins each rule above" (plan Goals line 43), including that a retry not deferred to the reset fails closed
  Expected change site: tests/test_usage_limit_resumes.py, test_is_limit_wait parametrize at lines 312-353 and test_a_limit_wait_that_also_asks_a_human_is_skipped parametrize at lines 265-285
  Evidence of absence: Neither test table includes (a) "Usage limit reached. Please retry the request. The limit resets later." (multi-clause bypass where deferral words in a separate sentence are treated as deferring the retry), (b) "Usage limit reached. Retry the request, not waiting until the limit resets." (multi-word negated deferral where "until" matches despite "not waiting"), or (c) "Usage limit reached. Please retry after the reset." (natural deferral using "after" which is omitted from LIMIT_DEFERRAL_PATTERN). The test suite passes while the compositional, negation, and missing-deferral-word bypasses remain undetected.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
